title: Blended SLA reconciliation and partial-credit remediation for Dedicated throughput
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a reconciled SLA for Dedicated capacity that (1) blends token-based throughput guarantees with tail-latency protections, (2) specifies error-budget consumption and partial-credit calculations, and (3) provides contract-ready language and operational runbooks for incidents and remediation.

Scope: measurement windowing and metric definitions (observed tokens/sec, sustained-slice throughput, 99.9th tail latency per model family), credit calculation for degraded performance (sliding-window, severity buckets), autoscaling and fleet-control triggers tied to contractual remediation, and monitoring/alerting integration with Console. Excludes per-tenant pricing changes and non-Dedicated product tiers.

Key deliverables:
- Precise metric definitions for throughput and latency (including model-variant mapping)
- Error-budget accounting model and examples (monthly reconciliation with sample math)
- Partial-credit schedule that maps severity -> % credit (zero to 100%) and remediation timeline
- Contract clause draft (customer-friendly and legal-ready)
- Operational playbook for detection, customer notice, and automated fallback/scale actions
- Console dashboard spec and billing reconciliation spreadsheet template

Measurement notes: We'll use the console trace pipeline (Prometheus-derived metrics augmented by request-level sampling via trace IDs) to compute per-tenant committed throughput vs observed sustained throughput in 5m and 1h windows. Tail latency is measured as 99.9th percentile across successful tokens for the same model family and input-size bucket. Blended SLA = max(throughput_score * 0.75 + latency_score * 0.25, 0) where score scales 0..1 per metric against the contractual target. Credits are computed monthly and applied to the next invoice or as usage credits for hosted add-ons.

acceptance_criteria: AC1: Console displays blended SLA score and per-metric breakdown for the last 30 days for any Dedicated tenant.
AC2: Monthly credit computation pipeline runs in sandbox and produces the spreadsheet used for billing reconciliation with sample tenant data.
AC3: Legal approves contract clause and sample customer notification language.
AC4: Autoscaling triggers linked to SLA degradation are documented and tested in staging (simulated overload).
AC5: Runbook created with RTO/RPO, roles, and escalation path; playbook validated in tabletop exercise.
decision_record: DR1: Use a blended metric (throughput 75% / latency 25%) to reflect Redwood's cost-first thesis while protecting tail-latency-sensitive workloads.
DR2: Compute credits monthly with sliding-window detection; credit % = severity bucket mapping to partial-credit table (see spreadsheet).
DR3: Credits are applied as usage/billing credits, not immediate refunds; legal prefers one-off invoices adjustments for enterprise customers.
DR4: For tenants below sampling threshold, fall back to per-request traces and apply a minimum-variance correction factor.
sample_contract_snippet: Redwood Inference will use best-effort production telemetry to measure Dedicated Throughput Commitments. If Redwood’s measured blended SLA (defined as 0.75 * throughput_score + 0.25 * latency_score) for a billing month falls below the committed threshold, Customer will be eligible for a service credit according to the severity table. Credits will be issued as usage credits or invoice adjustments and are Customer’s sole and exclusive remedy. Detailed measurement methodology is available in the Service Addendum.
